chunks: The dying one is more rightful with his wealth for as long as the soul is within him, distributing it. He (the Imam) said: Yes. So if he bequeaths by it, and if he exceeds, then there is nothing for him except the third.

key_terms.الثُّلُثُ: the third — the maximum one-third of an estate that can be willed away under Islamic law
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the dying person (al-mayyit) — one in the throes of death, not yet deceased
key_terms.يُبِينُ: to separate/distribute/allocate — specifically for the purpose of bequeathing

ai.seo_question: How much of one's wealth can a dying person bequest according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that a person retains full rights over their wealth while alive, even at the point of death. However, if a bequest is made that exceeds the permissible limit, only one-third of the estate may be distributed by will — a foundational principle of Islamic inheritance law. This ruling reflects the Quranic injunction to protect the rights of heirs while respecting the testator's limited right to dispose of property.
